title: The route out named for could-not-run attempts (revise) is refused at test-green, regression and static-checks
symbol: check_terminal / verify (could-not-run branch) / refused_runs; also shiploop_quality.check_terminal
scenario: Normal run with a bound Improve card. At test-green or regression the Until Loop completes (model's own run passed), then ShipLoop's own rerun times out or cannot start (for example the recorded command hangs under ShipLoop's closed stdin or 600s limit). The refusal says to report revise if the recorded command or budget is wrong. title: A skipped-on-budget command is deterministic, so a slow but passing suite becomes an unbounded could-not-run with no model-reachable fix
scenario: A step plan, system_commands or the end-of-work rerun lists several commands that each pass but total more than the 1800s per-invocation budget (regression and the end-of-work review run every command, and improve_changes.rerun_commands aggregates every completed item's commands). Each attempt runs the same ordered list, so the same tail commands are skipped every time: record disposition could-not-run, refused_runs stays 0, the cap never fires. Nothing is wrong in the environment and nothing hangs, yet the refusal says a hang in the item's own code is the model's to fix and blocked is only for user, grant or outside dependency. title: The 'report revise' route out of a repeated could-not-run is refused at test-green and regression, and the refusal never says how to get it accepted
scenario: Improve-bound run (every E2E run), work item at test-green or regression. The Until Loop completes normally, the model submits done, and ShipLoop's own rerun of a recorded command (a slow suite, or a watch-mode command) times out. The refusal says 'if the recorded command or its budget is itself wrong, report revise rather than retrying it' and records refused_runs=0. scenario: The Improve import at carry-forward calls verify with the pseudo-stage label. stage_spec gives carry-forward only done/repeat/blocked, so _remedy returns ''. After 7 product failures the refusal is 'done is no longer accepted for this action. Report blocked only if the user, an access grant or an outside dependency must unblock it.' Before that, each failure says 'Refused runs for this action: n of 7; after that the stage reports blocked', which tells the model that blocked is the end state for a plain test failure, contrary to the rule that a fixable problem is never blocked. A could-not-run attempt at this gate names no exit other than 'fix it', although the recorded commands come from earlier items' step plans and the model cannot change them there.
evidence: Ran probe_eow.py: first refusal ends 'Refused runs for this action: 1 of 7; after that the stage reports blocked.'. With 7 failed records the gate prints exactly the text above. The base text pointed at 'revise', which carry-forward also does not allow, so this is not new. A1 now pins the wording in test_a_label_that_is_not_a_graph_stage_has_no_remedy_and_does_not_raise.
suggested_fix: For a stage with no remedy outcome, drop 'after that the stage reports blocked'. Say plainly that the run-fixable failure must be fixed and that nothing else is accepted, or give the Improve review a…

title: stage_diff_lines reports a stage that was merely unmeasured on one side as 'only now' or 'only before', and gives no coverage note for the baseline side
scenario: The baseline row has `plan` with timing 'unavailable' (no turns key) and the new run measured plan. totals(before) omits plan, so the set difference prints 'only now: plan', implying plan is a newly visited stage; the 'covers N of M' note counts only skipped rows in `now`, so nothing says the baseline was partial. The reverse prints both the coverage note and 'only before: plan' although plan exists in `now`.
evidence: Ran stage_diff_lines([spec measured, plan unavailable], [spec, plan measured]) and got ['only now: plan']; with the arguments swapped got ['per-stage comparison covers 1 of 2 stages (1 had no measured timing)', 'only before: plan'].
suggested_fix: Compute the only-now/only-before sets over stage names present in either run (measured or not), and count unmeasured rows on both sides in the coverage line.

title: A recreated timeline.json yields confident stamps that per_stage treats as measured, producing fabricated zero-length stages
scenario: The engine's _updated_timeline recreates an unreadable or missing timeline.json and gives every historical action the same current time; the docstring of acceptance_stamps says a stamp 'can be a recovery artefact' and the design doc (A2 item 2) says to emit unavailable, never a confident zero. But the code only marks unavailable when a stamp is absent or unparsable; a recreated stamp parses fine. Example: a run resumed on an engine that predates timeline.json, or any run whose timeline was lost: history of N actions all stamped T; the first stage gets the whole span and turns, every other stage is reported measured with 0 seconds and 0 turns. Nothing flags the row set as suspect.
evidence: Synthetic run with three accepted actions all stamped 120s and started=120 (what _updated_timeline writes on recreation, read in shiploop_navigator.py): per_stage returned intake 20.0s/10 turns, spec 0.0s/0 turns, plan 0.0s/0 turns, none marked unavailable. Plausibility is low for a fresh run (all 11 recorded protocol-4 runs have a timeline), which is why this is minor.
suggested_fix: Treat a stamp as unavailable when it equals timeline `started` for any action after the first, or when several non-N/A actions share one stamp with a gap in runner events; mark the whole row set 'tim…

title: Seeded runs: first synthetic stage gets negative seconds, the other seeded stages are reported as measured zeros, and host start-up latency is billed to the first real stage
scenario: --seed-at step-plan records the stages before step-plan in one second at seed time, before the host launches; the runner's timeline.jsonl starts later. per_stage uses start = min(runner stamps) as the first row's lower bound, so the first seeded row has seconds = seed_stamp - start (negative). The other seeded rows have identical stamps and are reported as measured 0s/0 turns although the harness knows they are synthetic ('recorded without doing it'). The first real stage's window starts at the seed stamp, so the host launch gap is included. progress.py prints the negative value as minutes. Seeded runs write no baseline row, so the damage is confined to metrics.json/result.json/progress, but the change's stated aim is no fabricated timings. Non-monotonic stamps in general give negative seconds (no clamp).
evidence: Ran the real run.seed_run in a scratch directory (8 stages, all stamped within one second), then collect() with a host whose first event is 11s later: intake seconds -11.0 turns 0, the next seven rows 0.0s/0 turns each, incomplete step-plan row 17.0s for 4 turns spanning the launch gap. Synthetic non-monotonic stamps (105, 103) gave spec seconds -2.0.
suggested_fix: Mark rows whose action is in invocation.json seeded.skipped (or whose stamp precedes the first runner event) as timing 'unavailable'/'seeded', and start the first real window at the first runner even…

title: The incomplete row is missing or overstated in some stopped-run cases, and a halted run keeps no unaccepted stage (or reports the 'inner-loop' pseudo-label)
scenario: (a) A run that stopped before its first acceptance (host dies or times out in intake): per_stage returns [] at `if not accepted`, so no incomplete row exists, contrary to design item 3 (work after the last acceptance must not disappear); likewise when there is no runner timeline, the accepted rows are all unavailable and no incomplete row is added. (b) When the last accepted action has no stamp (timeline write lost, or a host kill between state.md and timeline.json in the store transaction, which writes state.md first), the `gap` rule is applied to accepted rows but not to the trailing incomplete row, so its window includes the unstamped action's work and is reported as measured. (c) pending_stage returns None for status halted, although the engine itself prints 'Stopped at: <stage> (unfinished)' and the packet offers a halt callback; termination_facts then falls back to the raw 'inner-loop' label for engine_stage and engine_unaccepted_stage is None.
evidence: Synthetic runs: collect([], events, status='active', stage='intake') gives stages []; accepted [A1 stamped, A2 unstamped] with pending plan gives an incomplete plan row of 8 turns / 8.0s that includes spec's turns; a halted inner-loop state gives pending_stage None and termination_facts engine_stage 'inner-loop'. Read per_stage, pending_stage and navigator.control/status_block.
suggested_fix: Emit the incomplete row even when nothing is accepted (window from the first runner event), carry `gap` into the incomplete row (mark it unavailable), and let pending_stage return the stage for halte…

title: progress.py hides the in-progress stage for the whole inner loop; its comment says the first line carries it, but that line prints the 'inner-loop' pseudo-stage
scenario: During a work item's build, which is most of a run, the run state's stage is the navigator's pseudo-label 'inner-loop'. metrics.pending_stage resolves it to the item's real stage (implement, test-green...) and per_stage produces an incomplete row, but report() filters incomplete rows out of 'accepted:' on the grounds that 'the in-progress stage is already on the first line from the run state'. The first line prints state.get('stage'), i.e. 'inner-loop', so the watching session never sees which stage is running.
evidence: progress.report on a synthetic active run with state stage 'inner-loop' and inner_loops W1.stage 'implement' printed '... active, rev 9, stage inner-loop, items 0/1' and 'accepted: intake ..., step-plan ...' with no mention of implement.
suggested_fix: Print metrics.pending_stage(state) (or the incomplete row's stage, turns and minutes) on the first line or as its own line, and keep it out of the accepted list.

title: Acceptance stamps are floored to whole seconds, so the turn that submits a stage's result lands in the next stage about a quarter of the time
scenario: The navigator's _utc_now truncates to %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. The assistant turn that calls `complete` has a runner stamp with a fractional part inside the truncated sliver (stamp, true acceptance time], so `previous < t <= item.t` excludes it and it is counted in the following stage. Every stage boundary has this bias, and stage_diff_lines prints any turn difference without a tolerance, so two identical runs print spurious stage differences of one turn. The old mtime attribution had sub-second precision (but jittered for other reasons), so this precision is a new loss.
evidence: On the real run v1190-hello-sonnet, of 13 located `complete` tool_use events, 3 had a runner stamp later than the engine's floor stamp for the action (+0.09s, +0.32s, +0.42s), so each of those turns is attributed to the next stage.
suggested_fix: Attribute by the completing turn (the turn whose tool call carries the action id) or give the boundary a one-second allowance (t <= stamp + 1); better, let the engine write sub-second stamps, which _…

title: A recreated or missing timeline.json is not detected; the stated 'never a confident zero' guarantee holds only for entries that are absent or unparseable
symbol: acceptance_stamps, per_stage; test helper write_engine_records docstring
scenario: The engine's _updated_timeline recreates a lost or malformed timeline.json and stamps every historical action with the current time (accepted.setdefault(action, now)). That produces readable, equal stamps, not missing ones. per_stage then gives the first stage the whole run and every later stage a measured 0.0 s / 0 turns (the fabricated zero the doc item 2 says to avoid). The test helper's docstring asserts the opposite ('an action with None gets no acceptance stamp, which is how an unreadable or recreated timeline looks to the reader'); acceptance_stamps' own docstring admits the artefact but does nothing. Related: with timeline.json absent and the run unfinished, every accepted row is unavailable but the incomplete row absorbs the entire run (probe: 40 turns / 39 s attributed to the pending stage), and with a trailing unstamped action plus a pending stage the incomplete row also covers the unstamped action's work (the gap flag is not consulted for the final row).
evidence: Probes: equal stamps -> rows [intake 30.0 s/31 turns, spec 0.0 s/0 turns, plan 0.0 s/0 turns] with no timing marker; missing timeline + active -> incomplete row seconds 39.0 turns 40; [A1 stamped, A2 unstamped] + pending -> incomplete row 29 s/29 turns. Read navigator _updated_timeline. Plausibility is low (needs a lost or pre-timeline run dir), hence minor.
suggested_fix: Treat stamps that equal timeline['started'] (or are all identical across several actions) as a recreation artefact and report those rows unavailable; honour the gap flag, and skip the incomplete row…

title: Stage rows for seeded runs carry negative or fabricated-looking seconds
scenario: A --seed-at run records its early stages through the engine before launching the host, so those engine stamps precede the first runner event. per_stage starts `since` at the first runner event, so the first seeded stage gets a negative duration and the others ~0 s / 0 turns, all labelled outcome done and measured; the first real stage then absorbs the seed-to-launch gap. progress.py prints these as e.g. '-1.7m'. Not baseline-feeding (seeded runs write no row) but it is in result.json/metrics.json and contradicts 'timing unavailable instead of invention'. Pre-existing in kind (old mtimes did the same) but not fixed by the change that claims to fix attribution.
evidence: Synthetic reproduction with stamps 100 s and 99 s before the first host event: intake seconds -100.0, spec 1.0, plan 119.0. Read run.py seed_run is called before launch. No recorded seeded run directory was available to confirm live.
suggested_fix: Report any acceptance stamped before the first host event as unavailable (seeded/synthetic) and start the first real window at that boundary.

title: Tests do not pin several A2 behaviours; the main-to-baseline wiring and the could_not_run count can regress silently
scenario: Behaviours changed by A2 that no test would catch if they broke: (a) metrics.verifications could_not_run: both assertions use 0, so a regex that never matches passes; (b) progress.py's incomplete-row filter and could-not-run line (the only progress test has no state); (c) wiring: dropping 'stages' from result['metrics'] in run.main, or dropping 'stages'/'termination' from baseline_row, leaves every test green while every later comparison silently prints 'per-stage comparison unavailable'. Also unpinned: that history order rather than stamp order is used when stamps are non-monotonic, and any non-Claude-shaped event stream (the source of the Codex findings above).
evidence: Mutation copy: could-not-run regex made unmatchable -> 20/20 StageAttribution/Baseline/Metrics tests OK; progress incomplete filter removed -> progress test OK; baseline_row without stages+termination -> 17 selected tests OK; result metrics without 'stages' -> 14 selected tests OK. By contrast dropping host from baseline_row, ignoring effort in previous_row, dropping the pending stage in collect,…
suggested_fix: Add a nonzero could_not_run verifications test, a progress.report test with an incomplete row, an assertion that a run through main writes baseline row['stages'] and result['metrics']['stages'], and…

title: Stage seconds are wall clock including interruption gaps, and stage turns jitter by about one per boundary; stage_diff_lines prints both without caveat or tolerance
scenario: seconds = acceptance stamp minus previous stamp, so a stage that spans a --resume-run gap, sleep or credit stop reports the gap as stage time; the doc (section 4.3 and A4 item 1) says time is confounded by interruption gaps and lists separating them under A2, but A2 does not. Separately the engine stamps have 1 s resolution (flooring) against float event times, so a stage's last turn is often credited to the next stage. stage_diff_lines prints any nonzero turn difference with no tolerance and shows minutes next to it, so ordinary run-to-run jitter appears as 'stage turns: ...'.
evidence: Re-ran collect on six recorded runs with the engine stamps moved by 1 s: turns shifted in 12 of 35, 10 of 35, 10 of 34, 12 of 34, 24 of 54 and 10 of 36 rows (about a third of rows by +-1). Read per_stage: no gap handling. No big idle gap occurred in the recorded Luna run (max event gap 8.7 min), so the gap effect is shown by code, not by data.
suggested_fix: Document stage turns as +-1 per boundary and have stage_diff_lines ignore differences of 1 turn (or report only the top moves above a stated tolerance); either exclude inter-session gaps from seconds…

title: A2 and A3 landed without the SPEC change-admission record, and the doc says they have no anchor

title: The merged tree now has a second per-stage time attribution (Run Review exporter), contradicting the doc's 'one implementation' claim
symbol: export_run stage loop (accepted.sort, _minutes(previous, moment)) versus metrics.per_stage
scenario: The doc ('Deduplication, resolved') says there is one attribution implementation, in metrics.py. After merging with the 1.19.0 line, export.py computes accept-to-accept minutes from the same state.md/timeline.json with different rules: sorted by stamp (history position only as tiebreak), first boundary the engine's 'started', unreadable stamps raise ExportError instead of reporting unavailable, no handling of a recreated timeline. run.py runs both on every run, so metrics.json and the review page can give different minutes for the same stage (S-12).
evidence: Read export.py lines ~560-600 and metrics.per_stage; run.py review_export is called for each run. Not executed, because the exporter writes into the run directory.
suggested_fix: Have the exporter reuse metrics.stage_results/per_stage output (or share one helper), or state in the doc that the exporter is a separate view with its own rules.

title: Second-resolution acceptance stamps push the completing turn into the next stage on about 30-45% of boundaries; zero-turn stage rows persist
scenario: The navigator's _utc_now truncates to the whole second, so a stamp is up to 1 s earlier than the true acceptance. per_stage uses `previous < t <= stamp`, so the turn that issued `shiploop complete` (about 0.5 s before acceptance) falls after the truncated stamp whenever the fraction of the second is small, and is credited to the next stage. In v1190-hello-sonnet skill-assess reports 5.0 s, 0 turns while skill-validate takes its turn (events at 191.37 and stamp 191, accept 191.87). Same symptom the older LEARNINGS note called 'boundary jitter', which this change was meant to remove. The tests use whole-second event times (100.0 + n) and whole-second stamps, so they cannot see it.
evidence: For the 3 Claude hello runs, against result-file mtimes (usable where mtime - stamp < 1 s), 7 of 26, 20 of 43 and 8 of 26 boundaries put exactly one turn in the wrong stage. Using stamp + 1.0 as the upper bound gives 0 wrong in all 95. Ran per_stage on the copies.
suggested_fix: Treat each stamp as the end of its second: bucket events with previous_stamp + 1 < t <= stamp + 1 (or add 0.5 s), and add a test with sub-second event times.

title: Seeded runs report negative seconds and credit the first real stage with the seed-to-launch gap
scenario: `--seed-at step-plan` records intake..plan through nav.save before the host starts, so their stamps precede the runner's first event. per_stage starts with `since = min(runner stamps)`, so the first seeded row gets seconds = stamp - start (negative), later seeded rows 0 s/0 turns as if measured, and the first real stage's window starts at the last seeded stamp, so it absorbs the whole seed-to-launch gap. Synthetic seeded run (seed 40 s before first event): intake seconds -40.0, test-spec 59.0 s instead of 20 s. progress.py would print '-0.7m'. Seeded runs write no baseline row, but metrics.json and result.json carry the rows.
evidence: Built a synthetic run whose first three history stamps are 40 s before the first event and ran metrics.collect; read SEED_SCRIPT in run.py. The old mtime code had the same artefact, so not a regression, but the change claims never to invent timing.
suggested_fix: Rows whose stamp precedes the first runner event should be marked timing 'unavailable' (or 'seeded') and the next measured row should start at the first runner event.

title: The unreadable-stamp guard does not cover the case the design names: a recreated timeline gives confident zeros; a run that dies in its first stage gets no incomplete row
scenario: Design item 2 says a recreated timeline stamps every historical action with the current time and must give 'unavailable, never a confident zero'. The engine never writes an unreadable stamp (it writes 'now'), so the t-is-None path is never reached. Synthetic recreated timeline (all four actions stamped at the end of a 600 s run): intake gets 60 turns/600 s, spec, plan and implement each get seconds 0.0, turns 0 as measured rows. Separately, per_stage returns [] when nothing was accepted, so a run dead in intake has no incomplete row although pending_stage says 'intake'.
evidence: Ran collect on both synthetic runs; read acceptance_stamps docstring ('a stamp can be a recovery artefact') and the early `if not accepted: return []`.
suggested_fix: Detect the recreated case (several actions share one stamp equal to the latest, or timeline.started not before the first accepted stamp with more than two actions) and mark all rows unavailable. Emit…

title: stage_diff_lines can mislead: unmeasured stages are reported as 'only before', coverage is reported for one side only, a failed or died baseline is summed in as if comparable
scenario: (a) Baseline fully measured, current run has plan/spec/test-strategy rows with timing unavailable: output is 'covers 31 of 34 stages (3 had no measured timing)' and then 'only before: plan, spec, test-strategy', which reads as if those stages were not run now. (b) If the baseline row has the unavailable rows instead, no coverage line is printed at all, though the diff is partial. (c) The coverage fraction divides distinct stage names by a row count. (d) previous_row takes the last matching row whatever its pass value (a row with pass false is returned), and baseline_stages keeps the incomplete row, which totals() sums into its stage: a baseline that died in verify (120 turns incomplete) prints 'verify 120->3 (15->0m)' and 'only now: carry-forward, handoff, ...' with no hint the baseline was incomplete. (e) Ranking is by turns only, so a pure time regression prints 'no per-stage turn difference'; minutes are rounded to whole minutes ('0->1m' for 30 s to 40 s). Also, since all 15 committed rows lack host/model/effort, the next run prints no baseline line at all, with no sentence saying comparable rows are absent.
evidence: Ran stage_diff_lines over real rows from v1190-hello-sonnet and -2 with the perturbations described and read the output; ran previous_row on a file with a pass:false row and effort:null row (both returned).
suggested_fix: Exclude incomplete rows (or name them) and unmeasured stages from the 'only before/now' sets, report coverage for both sides in row units, skip rows with pass false or an incomplete tail as baselines…

title: 'resume budget spent' is recorded without re-reading the engine state after the last resume
symbol: main (resume loop, `if resume_stop is None and host.resumable`)
scenario: The loop's while condition (`len(sessions) <= args.max_resumes`) ends it after the last permitted launch without grading the state that launch left. resume_stop stays None and becomes 'resume budget spent (N)' even if that last session finished the run (or left it blocked or halted), so the recorded reason is stale. With the default 20 it needs the 21st session to finish the run, which is rare, and the engine fields beside it say done. None of main()'s five resume_stop assignments is pinned: TerminationRecordTest passes literal resume_stop strings to termination_facts, and GrokResumeTest does not read result['termination'].
evidence: Ran fake Grok mode 'resume' with --max-resumes 1: the second session finished the run, yet termination was {engine_status done, resume_stop 'resume budget spent (1)'}. With no --max-resumes the same run records 'ShipLoop run is done'. Grep of test/shiploop-e2e.test.py shows no test of result['termination'], the baseline row's termination, or the stopped line.
suggested_fix: After the loop, grade the state once more and set resume_stop from it when the status is not active. Add a main()-level test per branch.

title: A halted run reports the navigator's 'inner-loop' root label as engine_stage and no unaccepted stage; status_reason is not recorded
scenario: pending_stage returns None for status 'halted' before it resolves the inner loop. termination_facts then falls back to engine.get('stage'), which is the pseudo-stage 'inner-loop'. A run halted while working an item gets engine_stage 'inner-loop' and engine_unaccepted_stage None, and the stopped line omits 'with X never accepted'. Active, paused and blocked runs in the same state resolve to the real stage. blocked, paused and halted states also carry a state.md `status_reason`, the engine's own recorded cause, and the record does not capture it. The 'engine halted' line therefore says nothing about why.
evidence: termination_facts called with {stage 'inner-loop', work_index 0, work_items [W1], inner_loops {W1: {stage 'test-green'}}} gave engine_stage 'test-green' with unaccepted 'test-green' for active, paused and blocked, but engine_stage 'inner-loop' with unaccepted None for halted. Navigator code read: _validate_current_state requires status_reason for paused/blocked/halted.
suggested_fix: Resolve the inner stage before the status early-return (halted still has an unfinished stage). Copy status_reason into the termination record.

title: After the merge no baseline row is comparable, including the two newest Claude hello rows, and a skipped comparison prints nothing

They include the 2026-10-04 hello rows added by 213dc8dc and 2e3e50e3 (per those commit messages, Claude Sonnet 5.5 verification runs), which landed after A2/A3's base. suggested_fix: Print one line when no comparable row exists (rows seen for the case, rows matching host/model/effort). Correct the '12 rows' wording. The 10-04 Claude Sonnet 5.5 hello rows could be backfilled with…

title: 'resume budget spent' is reported as the reason resuming stopped even when the last allowed session finished the run
symbol: main resume loop and 'if resume_stop is None and host.resumable'
scenario: The while condition len(sessions) <= args.max_resumes is false after the last permitted launch, so the loop never re-reads ShipLoop's state and resume_stop stays None. The fallback then asserts 'resume budget spent (N)' without checking anything. With --max-resumes 0 and a first session that completes the run, or any run that completes in its final permitted resume, the record claims the budget stopped it while the engine is done. The printed line reads 'no further resume: resume budget spent (0); engine done'. This is a guess presented as a fact, against the 'unknown rather than guessed' intent.
evidence: Fake Grok 'done' with --max-resumes 0 gave termination {sessions:1, resume_stop:'resume budget spent (0)', engine_status:'done'}. 'resume' with --max-resumes 1 gave sessions 2 and the same message with engine_status 'done'. Code read confirms the fallback is unconditional.
suggested_fix: After the loop, re-grade once and set resume_stop from the final state: 'ShipLoop run is <status>' when it is not active, and the budget message only when it is still active.

title: session_stops is not per session: a killed session has no entry, and the list spans more sessions than the counters beside it
symbol: termination_facts session_stops (built from metrics.collect sessions, one per result/end event)
scenario: Entries come only from result/end events, so a session killed by the harness timeout or the interrupt path adds none, and the code comment 'None means that session never reported one' cannot apply to it. Grok session 1 ends cleanly with the run active, and session 2 hangs and is killed at the deadline. title: Stage boundaries use whole-second engine stamps against millisecond event times
scenario: The navigator writes `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` (truncated down), while the runner stamps events to milliseconds. The assistant turn that submits `shiploop complete` is stamped before the CLI accepts, so when both fall in the same second the stamp can be earlier than that turn, and the closing turn is credited to the next stage. The effect is up to one turn per boundary, which matters for small stages and for 0 to 3 turn stage comparisons.
evidence: On /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261004/v1190-hello-sonnet the acceptance stamp trails the result file mtime by 0.24 to 1.0 s for 9 of the first 14 actions. 9 of 34 and 23 of 54 boundaries in the two 1.19.0 hello runs have a turn event inside (stamp, stamp+1 s].
suggested_fix: Treat a stamp as a one-second interval and attribute turns inside that second to the earlier stage, or note ±1 turn in the stage fields.

title: Stamps that are not acceptance instants give negative seconds and confident zeros; whole-second stamps shift boundary turns
scenario: (a) In a --seed-at run, the seeded stages are stamped when the harness seeded them, before the host's first event. The first seeded row gets seconds = stamp - first host event, which is negative. The other seeded rows get a confident 'seconds 0.0, turns 0'. The first real stage's window then starts at the seed time, so it is inflated by the host start-up. A2 says it will emit unavailable, never a confident zero, but only stamps that cannot be parsed are treated that way. A recreated timeline, where the engine stamps every historical action with 'now', would behave the same. (b) The engine stamps with %S resolution, truncated, and the host stamps are fractional, so turns arriving in the second after a truncated stamp are credited to the next stage. In the 1.19.0 hello gate run, 9 of 194 turns lie in that second, and skill-assess and product-acceptance show 0 turns over 5 s windows. Seeded runs write no baseline row, so this shows in result.json and progress output as, for example, '-0.1m'.

For (b), counted turns within (t, t+1] of each acceptance stamp on the v1190-hello-sonnet copy: 9 of 194. engine _utc_now uses strftime '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S…
suggested_fix: Mark an action timing 'unavailable' when its stamp precedes the first runner event or ties exactly with its predecessor's stamp. Say in the docstring that acceptance stamps carry up to 1 s of truncat…
